stories.title: My Happy Family
stories.text: My name is John. I am twenty-five years old. I live in a small house in Chicago. I have a large family. My father is a doctor at a local hospital. My mother is a teacher. She loves children very much. I have two sisters and one brother. We eat dinner together every evening. My sisters enjoy music, and my brother plays football. I love my family because they are kind and funny.

stories.title: The Lazy Cat
stories.text: I have a cat named Whiskers. He is very fat and orange. Whiskers sleeps all day long. He sleeps on the sofa, on the bed, and on the floor. He wakes up only for food. He likes fish and milk. When I return home from school, he looks at me and makes a noise. I play with him for ten minutes, but then he sleeps again. He is lazy but very cute.

stories.title: Sarah’s Morning Routine
stories.text: Sarah is a busy student. Every morning, she gets up at 6:30 AM. First, she drinks a glass of fresh water. Then, she cleans her teeth. She puts on her school clothes. For breakfast, she eats bread with cheese and drinks hot tea. At 7:30 AM, she walks to the bus station. The bus is yellow. She arrives at school at 8:00 AM. She is never late.

stories.title: The New Teacher
stories.text: Today is Monday. We have a new English teacher. Her name is Mrs. Green. She is tall and has brown hair. She comes from London. She speaks very clearly. In the classroom, she writes new words on the board. We read a book and write simple sentences. Mrs. Green is very friendly and helpful. She smiles a lot. I like her lessons because I learn many things.

stories.title: A Day at the Beach
stories.text: It is summer. The sun is hot and bright. Tom and his friends are at the beach. The sea is blue and clean. Tom swims in the water. His friend, Mike, plays a game on the sand. Lisa reads an interesting book. They are very happy. At 1:00 PM, they eat lunch together. They have sandwiches and cold drinks. Later, they make a big castle in the sand.

stories.title: My Favorite Hobby
stories.text: I like painting. It is my favorite activity. I have many colors: red, blue, green, and yellow. I paint on the weekends. Usually, I paint pictures of flowers and trees. Sometimes, I paint animals. My room is full of my art. My mother says, 'You are a good artist.' This makes me feel happy. I want to be famous in the future.

stories.title: The Big Supermarket
stories.text: Every Saturday, I go to the market with my dad. The shop is very large. There are many things to buy. First, we visit the fruit area. We buy apples, bananas, and oranges. Then, we go to the bakery. The bread smells fresh and good. My dad buys milk and eggs. I choose some chocolate. We pay for the food and go home in our car.

stories.title: London in Winter
stories.text: I live in London. In the winter, the weather is cold. It often rains. Sometimes, snow falls. When it snows, the city looks white and beautiful. People wear warm coats and hats. I like drinking hot drinks in winter. I stay inside my house and watch films. The days are short, and the nights are long. I prefer the snow to the rain.

stories.title: The Little Coffee Shop
stories.text: There is a small café near my office. Its name is 'The Bean.' I go there every morning. The place smells like fresh coffee. There are five tables and soft chairs. The owner is an old man named Mr. Brown. He knows my name. I always ask for a cappuccino. I sit near the window and look at the people outside. It is a quiet and nice place.

stories.title: Learning Guitar
stories.text: David wants to play the guitar. He has a new instrument. It is brown and looks nice. He takes lessons every Tuesday. His fingers hurt, but he practices every day. He plays easy songs. His neighbors hear the music. David is not perfect, but he tries hard. He wants to play a song for his girlfriend. He is very excited about it.

stories.title: The Last Holiday
stories.text: Last summer, my family and I traveled to Spain. We went by plane. It was my first time on a plane, so I felt a bit nervous. But the journey was smooth. We stayed in a lovely hotel near the coast. The weather was fantastic every day. We swam in the ocean and ate local food. One night, we watched a traditional dance show. It was the best holiday of my life.

stories.title: A Surprise Party
stories.text: Yesterday was my sister’s birthday. We planned a surprise party for her. I invited all her friends. My mother baked a huge chocolate cake. We hid in the living room. When she opened the door, we shouted, 'Surprise!' She was shocked and happy. She cried a little because she is emotional. We danced and celebrated until midnight.

stories.title: The Lost Wallet
stories.text: Last week, Mark lost his wallet at the shopping center. He went into a shoe shop and tried on some trainers. When he went to pay, he realized his wallet was missing. He was very worried. He searched everywhere. Fortunately, a kind lady found it on a seat and gave it to the staff. Mark was relieved and thanked the woman.

stories.title: Moving to a New City
stories.text: Next month, I am going to move to New York. I found a new job there as an architect. I am very excited, but also a bit sad to leave my friends. I am going to rent a small apartment in Brooklyn. I have already started packing my boxes. My friends offered to help me this weekend. It is a fresh start in my life.

stories.title: A Strange Dream
stories.text: Two nights ago, I had a very strange dream. In my dream, I could fly over my town. I landed on a cloud made of sweet candy. Suddenly, a giant bird appeared and said, 'Wake up!' Then I opened my eyes. It was 7:00 AM and my alarm was ringing. I felt tired but amused by the funny dream.

stories.title: The Broken Car
stories.text: On Saturday, Mr. Smith wanted to drive to the countryside. He got into his car, but the engine did not start. He checked under the hood, but he didn't know how to fix it. He called a mechanic. The mechanic arrived an hour later and repaired the problem quickly. It was just a dead battery. Mr. Smith was late, but he still enjoyed his day.

stories.title: First Day at the Gym
stories.text: Alice decided to get fit and joined a sports center. Yesterday was her first session. A trainer named Mike assisted her. He showed her how to use the running machine. Alice ran for twenty minutes. She was exhausted and her face was red. Then she lifted some weights. Today, her muscles are painful, but she feels positive. She is going to go again tomorrow.

stories.title: Cooking Dinner
stories.text: Last night, I invited my friends for dinner. I planned to cook pasta. I boiled the water and prepared the vegetables. However, I added too much salt to the sauce! It tasted terrible. I quickly made a new sauce. Luckily, the second one was delicious. My friends loved the meal and we had a wonderful conversation about our jobs and hobbies.

stories.title: The Rainy Picnic
stories.text: Last Sunday, we organized a picnic. The weather forecast predicted sun. We drove to the forest and started eating. Suddenly, dark clouds appeared and it rained heavily. We ran to the car quickly. We were completely wet. We ate our sandwiches inside the vehicle. Ideally, picnics are for sunny days, but this one was funny.

stories.title: A Letter to a Friend
stories.text: Dear Julie, I am writing this letter from Paris. I arrived here three days ago. The city is amazing. I visited the Eiffel Tower yesterday. It is huge. The view from the top was incredible. I also drank coffee in a popular café. I am going to stay here for one more week. I bought a present for you. See you soon! Love, Anna.

stories.title: The Job Interview
stories.text: Julia has worked as a graphic designer for three years. She recently applied for a position at a famous technology company. Yesterday was the interview. She felt nervous, but she answered the questions confidently. She explained how she had solved problems in her previous role. At the end, the manager smiled. Julia feels relieved now. She might get the job, or she might not, but she did her best.

stories.title: An Unexpected Adventure
stories.text: Last weekend, Mike went camping. In the middle of the night, a strange noise woke him up. It sounded like a wild animal! He was terrified. He woke his friends up immediately. Suddenly, a small cat walked into their tent. They all laughed. It wasn't a bear; it was just a hungry stray cat. They gave the cat some food. It was a frightening but amusing experience.

stories.title: The Health Resolution
stories.text: Since the beginning of the year, Tom has decided to lose weight. He has stopped eating unhealthy food and sugar. It hasn't been easy because he loves chocolate. However, he has already lost five kilograms. He goes running three times a week. If he continues this routine, he will be much healthier by summer. He feels more energetic than before.

stories.title: Learning to Drive
stories.text: Sarah has been taking driving lessons for two months. Driving in the city is stressful because there is heavy traffic. Yesterday, she had to park in a very small space. She tried three times. Finally, she succeeded. Her instructor told her she should be more patient. She is going to take her driving test next week. She hopes she will pass.

stories.title: A Weekend in Paris
stories.text: Mark has just returned from a short trip to Paris. He visited the Louvre Museum, which he found incredibly impressive. He wanted to see the Mona Lisa, but the crowd was too large. Instead, he explored the streets of Montmartre. He tasted authentic French pastries. He mentioned that he would love to live there one day if he could speak French fluently.

stories.title: The Friendly Neighbor
stories.text: When I moved to my new apartment, I didn't know anybody. One day, my neighbor, Mrs. Wilson, knocked on my door. She brought me a homemade apple pie. We started talking and realized we both love gardening. Since then, we have become good friends. She helps me water my plants when I am away. It is nice to have neighbors you can trust.

stories.title: The Cooking Contest
stories.text: Liam entered a local cooking competition last Saturday. He decided to make his grandmother's secret soup recipe. He was competing against five other chefs. During the contest, he burned his hand slightly, but he continued cooking. The judges tasted his soup and loved it. Although he didn't win the first prize, he received a special award for creativity. He was very proud of his achievement.

stories.title: The Lost Dog
stories.text: Walking in the park, Jenny found a dog without a collar. It looked lost and hungry. She couldn't leave it there, so she took it home. She posted a photo of the dog on social media. Two hours later, a man contacted her. He was crying with joy. The dog was his best friend. When they met, the dog jumped happily. Jenny felt great about helping them.

stories.title: Buying a Used Car
stories.text: Kevin needs a vehicle for his new job. He doesn't have enough money for a new one, so he has been looking for a used car. He found a blue sedan online. The owner said it was in good condition. Kevin went to inspect it yesterday. The engine sounded good, but the tires were old. He offered a lower price, and the owner agreed. Kevin is satisfied with the deal.

stories.title: The Stressful Exam
stories.text: Maria has been studying for her final biology exam for weeks. She has read the textbook twice and prepared many revision cards. She feels tired and stressed. Her mother advised her to take a break and sleep. Maria knows she is right. If she doesn't sleep, she won't be able to concentrate tomorrow. She plans to watch a movie tonight to relax.

stories.title: The Mystery of the Old Library
stories.text: While Elena was researching local history, she discovered a dusty book hidden behind a shelf. It contained letters from the 19th century written by a woman named Clara. Elena realized Clara had hidden a treasure. After interpreting the clues, Elena dug near the clock tower and found a box of gold coins. She decided the treasure should be donated to the museum for everyone to see.

stories.title: A Digital Detox
stories.text: James, a software engineer, realized he was addicted to his smartphone. He felt exhausted and burned out. Consequently, he decided to attempt a digital detox for a week. The first few days were challenging, but by the fourth day, he started to appreciate the beauty of the world around him. He read books and painted. He recognized that technology shouldn't control his life.

stories.title: Noise Pollution
stories.text: Living in the city center has its advantages, but the constant noise is a major disadvantage. Sarah has been struggling to sleep due to the construction work nearby. She has filed a formal complaint with the council, yet nothing has changed. She is considering moving to the suburbs. Although she would miss the convenience of the city, her peace of mind is more important.

stories.title: The Freelancer Lifestyle
stories.text: After quitting his corporate job, Tom became a freelance writer. Initially, he struggled to manage his time efficiently. He would often work late into the night. However, he has now established a strict routine. The freedom to work from any location is amazing. Next month, he intends to work from a beach house in Bali, which has always been his ambition.

stories.title: The Cancelled Flight
stories.text: We were supposed to fly to London yesterday, but our flight was cancelled due to a severe storm. We were stranded at the airport for ten hours. The airline staff were overwhelmed and couldn't provide accurate information. Eventually, we were given a hotel room. It was a frustrating experience, but we met a lovely couple and played cards with them all night.

stories.title: The Charity Event
stories.text: Organizing the charity gala was a significant responsibility for Linda. She had to coordinate catering, music, and guest lists. There were moments when she wanted to give up. However, on the night of the event, everything proceeded smoothly. They raised over fifty thousand dollars for the local hospital. Linda felt a deep sense of accomplishment seeing the community come together.

stories.title: The Ambitious Project
stories.text: The company has launched a new project aimed at reducing plastic waste. As the project manager, David is responsible for its success. He has been working overtime to ensure all deadlines are met. Although the budget is limited, the team is highly motivated. If they succeed, it will revolutionize the industry. David is optimistic that their hard work will result in success.

stories.title: Misunderstanding at Work
stories.text: A serious misunderstanding occurred between two departments yesterday. The marketing team thought the design team had finalized the brochures, but they hadn't. This caused a delay in the launch. A meeting was held to resolve the issue. It turned out that an email had been sent to the wrong address. They agreed to improve their communication channels to avoid future errors.

stories.title: Benefits of Yoga
stories.text: Clara used to think yoga was only for flexible people. However, after suffering from back pain, she was advised to try it. She has been attending classes for six months now. Not only has her pain disappeared, but she also feels much calmer. She realized that yoga is as much about mental strength as it is about physical flexibility.

stories.title: Historical Documentary
stories.text: I watched a fascinating documentary about the Industrial Revolution last night. It explained how the invention of the steam engine changed society forever. While it brought economic growth, it also caused terrible pollution and poor working conditions. The documentary interviewed historians who argued that we are still dealing with the consequences of that era today. It was very educational.

stories.title: The Dilemma of Progress
stories.text: The village of Oakhaven was on the verge of significant change due to a proposed hydroelectric dam. Supporters argued it would generate clean energy and employment. However, environmentalists raised valid concerns about the ecosystem. 'It’s a difficult situation,' the mayor admitted. Had the council consulted residents earlier, the negative reaction might not have been so severe. The village stood at a critical turning point.

stories.title: A Twist of Fate
stories.text: Julian was a careful planner, poised to become a partner at his law firm. Yet, getting stuck in an elevator with an eccentric artist named Leo changed everything. Their conversation evolved into a profound therapy session. Julian realized he was pursuing a career that did not suit him. He quit his job to pursue culinary arts, a decision that liberated his spirit.

stories.title: Implications of AI
stories.text: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has sparked a heated debate regarding ethics and employment. While some hail it as the beginning of a new era of productivity, others fear the displacement of the workforce. It is essential that we establish robust regulations. Unless we address these concerns proactively, the societal gap could widen, leading to unforeseen consequences.

stories.title: The Fragility of Democracy
stories.text: History has repeatedly demonstrated that democracy is not a static state but a constant endeavor. Recent political instability has exposed the weaknesses in our institutions. The division of the electorate, fueled by false information, threatens the very fabric of society. Only by encouraging critical thinking and polite discourse can we hope to bridge this gap and preserve our democratic values.

stories.title: The Nuances of Negotiation
stories.text: Successful negotiation is less about aggression and more about empathy. During the merger discussions, the CEO displayed remarkable skill. Rather than imposing demands, she listened to the opposing party's complaints. This approach not only reduced tension but also paved the way for a mutually beneficial agreement. It was a demonstration of diplomacy that few could have executed so perfectly.

stories.title: The Paradox of Choice
stories.text: In modern society, we are led to believe that more choice equates to more freedom. Psychologically, however, an abundance of options often leads to inability to act and dissatisfaction. When faced with endless possibilities, we fear making the wrong decision. This phenomenon suggests that simplifying our lives might actually be the key to genuine satisfaction.

stories.title: Aesthetics of Minimalism
stories.text: The minimalist movement is a reaction against the consumer culture that defines success by accumulation. By removing the non-essential, one creates space for mental clarity. It is not merely a design choice but a lifestyle philosophy. Those who embrace it often report a profound sense of freedom, having released themselves from the burden of material possessions.

stories.title: The Burden of Leadership
stories.text: Leadership is often idealized, yet the reality is filled with isolation. The CEO had to make the painful decision to reduce the size of the company to save it from failure. He bore the weight of hundreds of livelihoods on his shoulders. It is in these critical moments that true character is revealed, distinguishing a mere manager from a true leader.

stories.title: Intricacies of Law
stories.text: The legal case was a maze of complexities, challenging even the most experienced attorneys. The defense argued that the law was unclear and open to interpretation. The prosecution, conversely, relied on a strict adherence to previous cases. The judge's ruling would set a standard for future cases, highlighting how the law is a living entity, constantly evolving with societal norms.

stories.title: Evolution of Social Norms
stories.text: What was considered unacceptable a decade ago is now commonplace, illustrating the fluidity of social norms. This shift is largely driven by the younger generation's refusal to accept the current state of affairs. They challenge traditional structures and demand inclusivity. While this rapid change unsettles some, it is the engine of progress, pushing society towards a more fair future.

stories.title: The Echoes of Silence
stories.text: In the grand theater of existence, silence is a powerful presence. Eleanor, a linguist studying dying dialects, understood that words are merely a surface layer. Upon returning to the metropolis, she felt acute dislocation. She found comfort in old bookshops. Her theory argued that true understanding arises not from what is spoken, but from what is left unsaid, challenging contemporary linguistic theory.

stories.title: The Architect of Dreams
stories.text: Elias perceived the skyline as a living organism. His project, the 'Nebula Spire,' was deemed impossible by practical peers. Undeterred, he labored to integrate advanced materials reflecting the city's emotional state. As the Spire pulsed with violet light at twilight, it captivated the citizens. Elias proved architecture could be a catalyst for collective thought, blurring the physical and philosophical.

stories.title: The Labyrinth of Consciousness
stories.text: To explore the human mind is to navigate a maze with no exit. The philosopher spent his life contemplating the nature of self-awareness. He proposed that consciousness is not a single entity but a collection of perceptions held together by the fragile thread of memory. His significant work challenged the dualism that had dominated Western thought for centuries.

stories.title: The Symphony of Chaos
stories.text: The market crash was not an irregularity but a symphony of chaos conducted by invisible hands. Analysts scrambled to impose a story upon the unpredictable nature of the event. Yet, in the midst of the financial ruin, a strange beauty emerged—the resilience of the human spirit. It served as a stark reminder that our structures of order are merely temporary defenses against the tide of disorder.

stories.title: Ephemeral Nature of Power
stories.text: History is filled with the remains of empires whose leaders believed their rule was eternal. The dictator sat in his luxurious palace, unaware of the whispers of opposition that would soon grow into revolution. Power, he failed to realize, is temporary, slipping through one's fingers the tighter one grasps it. His inevitable fall was a testament to the excessive pride of mankind.

stories.title: Allegory of the Cave
stories.text: In a digital age, Plato's allegory of the cave resonates with terrifying accuracy. We are held not by chains, but by algorithms that curate our reality. The shadows on the wall have been replaced by pixels on a screen. To step outside and witness the blinding light of truth requires an intellectual courage that few possess, preferring the comfortable safety of their own echo chamber.

stories.title: The Tapestry of Fate
stories.text: The novelist viewed life as a woven fabric, where every thread of interaction is placed with intention. She rejected the notion of coincidence. In her latest masterpiece, the protagonist's seemingly random encounter is revealed to be the central point upon which the entire plot pivots. Her writing is a meditation on the connection of all things, urging the reader to look beyond the surface.

stories.title: Quiet Desperation
stories.text: Thoreau’s observation that the majority of men lead lives of quiet desperation hangs over the modern corporate landscape like a shadow. The protagonist, a small part in the bureaucratic machine, finds his soul slowly eroded by the monotony. His rebellion is not loud but internal—a refusal to let his imagination be taken over by the mundane. It is a moving exploration of existential resistance.

stories.title: Illusion of Control
stories.text: We build barriers and dams, draft laws and treaties, all in a desperate attempt to assert control over a chaotic universe. The hurricane that devastated the coast was a humbling rejection of this arrogance. In the aftermath, the community did not rebuild the walls higher but learned to move with the environment. It was a fundamental shift from domination to coexistence.

stories.title: Resonance of History
stories.text: Walking through the ancient ruins, one can almost hear the echoes of history—the whispers of forgotten lovers and the shouts of long-dead soldiers. The site serves as a record, where layers of civilization are written over one another. It compels the observer to contemplate their own smallness in the vast continuum of time, evoking a sense of deep sadness and beauty.

stories.title: My Best Friend
stories.text: My best friend is Emma. She is eleven years old, like me. We are in the same class at school. Emma has long black hair and brown eyes. She is very funny and kind. Every day, we walk to school together. After school, we do our homework at her house. Her mother makes us sandwiches. On Saturdays, we play tennis in the park. I am happy because I have a good friend.

stories.title: A Rainy Sunday
stories.text: Today is Sunday, and it is raining. I cannot go outside. My brother and I are at home with our parents. My father reads a book on the sofa. My mother cooks soup in the kitchen. My brother and I play a game on the floor. Then we watch a film together. The soup is hot and very good. I like rainy days at home with my family.

stories.title: At the Doctor
stories.text: Ben is ill today. He has a bad cold and his head hurts. His mother takes him to the doctor. The doctor is a tall woman with glasses. She looks at his throat and listens to his chest. "You need to rest," she says. "Drink a lot of water and stay in bed for two days." Ben goes home and sleeps. The next day, he feels better.

stories.title: Grandma's Garden
stories.text: My grandmother lives in a small house near the sea. She has a beautiful garden. There are red flowers, yellow flowers, and a big apple tree. Every summer, I visit her for two weeks. In the morning, we water the plants together. In the afternoon, we sit under the tree and drink cold juice. Grandma tells me stories about her life. I love her garden.

stories.title: The School Bus
stories.text: Every morning, Lucy takes the school bus. The bus stops in front of her house at half past seven. The driver is a friendly man called Mr. Jones. He always says, "Good morning!" Lucy sits next to her friend Mia. They talk and laugh on the way to school. The journey takes twenty minutes. In the afternoon, the same bus brings them home.

stories.title: Tom's Birthday
stories.text: Today is Tom's birthday. He is seven years old. His parents have a small party for him at home. Six friends from school come to the party. They play games in the garden and eat cake and ice cream. Tom gets many presents. His favourite present is a red bike from his grandparents. In the evening, Tom is tired but very happy.

stories.title: Lunch in the Park
stories.text: It is a sunny day, and Anna has lunch in the park. She works in an office near the park. At twelve o'clock, she takes her bag and goes outside. She sits on a bench under a tree. She eats a sandwich and an orange. Children play football on the grass, and birds sing in the trees. After forty minutes, Anna goes back to work.

stories.title: My Bedroom
stories.text: My bedroom is small, but I love it. The walls are light blue. There is a bed next to the window. Near the bed, there is a desk and a chair. I do my homework at the desk. On the wall, there are photos of my family and my friends. I have a lot of books on a shelf. At night, I read a book before I sleep.

stories.title: New Shoes
stories.text: Sam needs new shoes for school. His old shoes are too small. On Saturday, he goes to a shoe shop with his mother. There are many shoes in the shop. Sam likes a pair of black shoes. He tries them on, and they are comfortable. His mother asks, "How much are they?" "Forty dollars," says the woman in the shop. They buy the shoes and go home.

stories.title: Morning on the Farm
stories.text: Peter lives on a farm with his family. Every day, he gets up at five o'clock. First, he gives food to the cows and the chickens. Then he gets the eggs from the chickens. His sister helps him. After that, the family has a big breakfast in the kitchen. They eat eggs, bread, and cheese. The farm is hard work, but Peter loves it.

stories.title: My Little Brother
stories.text: I have a little brother. His name is Leo, and he is four years old. Leo has big blue eyes and short brown hair. He likes cars and trains. Every morning, he wakes me up at six o'clock. He jumps on my bed and says, "Play with me!" Sometimes he is noisy, but he is very sweet. I read stories to him at night. I love my little brother.

stories.title: A Day at the Zoo
stories.text: On Sunday, Mia goes to the zoo with her class. The zoo is big, and there are many animals. First, they see the lions. The lions are sleeping in the sun. Then they visit the monkeys. The monkeys are funny, and the children laugh. Mia's favourite animal is the elephant. It is very big and grey. At the end of the day, everyone is tired but happy.

stories.title: A Cold Winter Day
stories.text: It is very cold today. There is snow on the ground and on the trees. Max puts on his warm coat, his hat, and his gloves. He goes outside with his sister. They make a snowman in the garden. It has a carrot for a nose. After an hour, their hands are cold. They go inside, and their mother makes hot chocolate for them.

stories.title: My Dog Rex
stories.text: I have a dog. His name is Rex. He is three years old, and he is black and white. Rex is very friendly. He likes people and other dogs. Every evening, I take him for a walk in the park. He runs after the ball and brings it back to me. Rex eats twice a day. At night, he sleeps in a small bed in the kitchen.

stories.title: Our Kitchen
stories.text: Our kitchen is my favourite room in the house. It is big and bright. There is a large table in the middle. We eat breakfast and dinner there. My mother likes cooking, and the kitchen always smells nice. There is a big window, and we can see the garden. On Sundays, my father makes pancakes. We sit at the table together and talk.

stories.title: At the Library
stories.text: Every Thursday, Nina goes to the library after school. The library is quiet and has thousands of books. Nina loves stories about animals. She chooses two or three books every week. The librarian is a kind woman. She helps Nina find good books. Nina sits at a table near the window and reads for an hour. Then she takes the books home.

stories.title: Riding a Bike
stories.text: Lily is six years old. Today, she is learning to ride a bike. Her father holds the back of the bike, and Lily starts to move. Her father says, "Don't stop!" Lily rides slowly down the street. Her father lets go of the bike, but Lily does not know. She rides alone for the first time! She is very proud of herself.

stories.title: A Busy Mother
stories.text: My mother is a nurse at a hospital. She works very hard. She gets up early and makes breakfast for us. Then she drives to work. At the hospital, she helps sick people all day. In the evening, she comes home and cooks dinner. After dinner, she checks our homework. She is always busy, but she always has time for us.

stories.title: The New Phone
stories.text: Jack has a new phone. It is a present from his parents. The phone is small and black, and it has a big screen. Jack takes photos of his friends and his cat. He sends messages to his cousin in Canada. But his parents have a rule: no phone at dinner and no phone after nine o'clock. Jack thinks this is a good rule.

stories.title: Breakfast Time
stories.text: In my family, breakfast is an important meal. We have breakfast at seven o'clock every morning. My father drinks coffee, and my mother drinks tea. My sister and I drink milk or orange juice. We usually eat bread with butter and jam. Sometimes we have eggs and cheese. At the weekend, we eat breakfast late and talk for a long time.

stories.title: The Train to the City
stories.text: Every Friday, Emma takes the train to the city. She visits her aunt there. The train leaves at nine o'clock in the morning. Emma buys a ticket at the station and waits on the platform. The train is fast and clean. Emma sits by the window and looks at the fields, the trees, and the small villages. The journey takes one hour. Her aunt waits for her at the station.

stories.title: The Football Match
stories.text: It is Saturday afternoon. Daniel and his father are at a big football game. Their favourite team is playing today. There are thousands of people, and everyone is wearing red shirts. The players run out, and the people sing. After twenty minutes, their team gets the first goal! Daniel and his father stand up and sing. At the end, their team wins two to one. They go home very happy.

stories.title: A Letter from Grandpa
stories.text: Ella gets a letter today. It is from her grandfather. He lives in a small town far away. In the letter, he writes about his garden and his old dog. He also asks about Ella's school. At the end, he writes, "I miss you. Please visit me in the summer." Ella smiles. She takes a pen and some paper and starts her answer.

stories.title: The Small Village
stories.text: Carlos lives in a small village in the mountains. There are only fifty houses in the village. There is one school, one shop, and a small church. Everyone knows everyone. In the morning, the air is fresh and cold. Carlos walks to school with his friends. In the evening, people sit outside their houses and talk. Carlos loves the quiet life in his village.

stories.title: At the Hotel
stories.text: Mr. and Mrs. Wood are on holiday. They arrive at a hotel near the beach. The woman at the desk smiles and says, "Welcome!" She gives them the key to their room. The room is on the third floor. It has a big bed, a small table, and a balcony. From the balcony, they can see the sea. "This is perfect," says Mrs. Wood.

stories.title: My Job at the Café
stories.text: My name is Sofia, and I am a student. At the weekend, I work in a small café. I start at eight o'clock in the morning. I make coffee and tea, and I carry food to the tables. Some customers are very friendly. They talk to me and say thank you. The work is not easy, but I like it. I save my money for a new computer.

stories.title: Autumn Colours
stories.text: It is October, and autumn is here. The leaves on the trees are red, orange, and yellow. Every day, more leaves fall to the ground. The weather is cooler, and it often rains. Children walk to school in their coats and boots. They love to jump in the leaves. In the park, people take photos of the beautiful colours. Autumn is my favourite season.

stories.title: A Walk by the River
stories.text: On Sunday morning, Paul and his wife walk by the river. The weather is warm and sunny. There are ducks on the water, and some children give them bread. Paul and his wife walk for an hour. Then they stop at a small café. They drink coffee and eat a piece of cake. They sit in the sun and watch the boats on the river.

stories.title: The Swimming Lesson
stories.text: Hana is eight years old, and she cannot swim. Every Tuesday, she has a swimming lesson at the pool near her school. Her teacher is a young man called Adam. He is very patient. First, Hana learns to put her face in the water. Then she learns to move her arms and legs. After ten lessons, Hana can swim across the pool!

stories.title: Making a Cake
stories.text: Today is Mother's Day. Tom and his sister want to make a cake for their mother. Their father helps them in the kitchen. They put sugar, eggs, butter, and milk in a big bowl. Tom and his sister use a big spoon. Then their father puts the cake in the oven for forty minutes. The kitchen smells very good. Their mother is very happy with her present.

stories.title: The Lost Key
stories.text: It is eight o'clock in the morning, and Olivia is late for work. She cannot find her key. It is not in her bag or on the table. She looks under the sofa and in the kitchen. Then she calls her husband. "Look in your coat," he says. Olivia puts her hand in her coat, and the key is there! She laughs and runs to the bus stop.

stories.title: A School Day
stories.text: Ali is ten years old, and he goes to a big school in the city. His first lesson is at nine o'clock. On Mondays, he has English, maths, and art. English is his favourite lesson. At lunchtime, he eats with his friends in the school garden. In the afternoon, they play basketball. School finishes at half past three, and Ali walks home with his sister.

stories.title: The Museum Trip
stories.text: Today, Mrs. Brown's class is at the city museum. The museum is very old and very big. The children see old coins, pictures, and a very big dinosaur. The dinosaur is their favourite. A man tells them about the history of the city. The children listen and ask many questions. At the end of the visit, they buy postcards in the museum shop.

stories.title: Pizza Night
stories.text: Every Friday is pizza night in the Garcia family. Mr. Garcia makes the food at home, and the children help him. Maria puts tomatoes on the bread, and her brother puts cheese and vegetables on it. Then Mr. Garcia cooks it for fifteen minutes. The kitchen smells very good! The family eats together in front of the TV and watches a film. It is their favourite night of the week.

stories.title: At the Post Office
stories.text: Mr. Evans wants to send a small box to his son in Australia. He goes to the post office in the town centre. There are five people in the line. He waits for ten minutes. Then a young woman asks, "Can I help you?" He gives her the box, and she puts it on a scale. "That is twelve pounds," she says. Mr. Evans pays and says thank you.

stories.title: A New Friend
stories.text: Kenji is from Japan, and he is new at the office. He does not know anyone. At lunchtime, he eats alone. On Wednesday, a woman sits at his table. "Hi, I am Laura," she says. "Where are you from?" They talk about their countries, their families, and their favourite food. Now they have lunch together every day. Kenji is happy because he has a new friend.

stories.title: The Night Sky
stories.text: It is a warm summer night. Leo and his grandfather are in the garden. They sit on the grass and look up. It is dark, and there are hundreds of stars. The moon is big and white. His grandfather knows the names of many stars. He shows Leo the brightest star. Leo thinks the night is very beautiful, and he does not want to go to bed.

stories.title: The Music Class
stories.text: On Thursday afternoons, Sara has a music class at school. Her music teacher is Mr. Lee. He plays the piano very well. In the class, the children sing songs together. Some children play small drums, and others play the guitar. Sara likes singing more than playing an instrument. Next month, the class has a small concert for the parents. Sara is a little nervous, but happy.

stories.title: Grandpa's Old Car
stories.text: My grandfather has a very old car. It is green, and it is forty years old. The car is slow and noisy, but he loves it. He washes it every Sunday. Sometimes he takes me for a drive in the country. We open the windows and listen to old songs on the radio. People look at the car and smile. I love our drives together.

stories.title: A Visit to the Dentist
stories.text: Emily has a pain in her tooth. Her mother calls the dentist, and they go there in the afternoon. Emily is a little afraid. The dentist is a friendly man. He says, "Open your mouth, please." He looks at her teeth with a small light. "It is not a big problem," he says. After twenty minutes, the pain is gone. Emily feels much better.

stories.title: The Missed Bus
stories.text: Yesterday, Daniel woke up late because his alarm clock did not ring. He got dressed quickly and ran to the bus stop without breakfast. When he arrived, the bus was already leaving. He waved his arms, but the driver did not see him. The next bus was thirty minutes later, so Daniel decided to walk. It was a long way, and he arrived at work at ten o'clock. His boss was not angry, but Daniel bought a new alarm clock that evening.

stories.title: A Day Without Electricity
stories.text: Last Saturday, there was no electricity in our town from morning until evening. At first, my children were bored because they could not watch TV or use the computer. We could not cook lunch either, so we ate bread, cheese and fruit. In the afternoon, we played cards and board games together. In the evening, we lit candles and told stories. When the lights came back, my son said, "That was the best day of the holidays!"

stories.title: Shopping for a Present
stories.text: Next week is my sister's birthday, so I went to the shopping centre on Sunday to buy her a present. First, I looked at some jumpers, but they were too expensive. Then I went into a bookshop. My sister loves cooking, and I found a beautiful book with recipes from Italy. It cost twenty pounds. The shop assistant wrapped it in red paper for me. I think my sister is going to love it.

stories.title: The Camping Trip
stories.text: Last summer, Emma and her friends went camping near a lake. They took two tents, warm clothes and a lot of food. On the first day, they swam in the lake and walked in the forest. In the evening, they made a fire and cooked sausages. At night, it started to rain heavily, and water came into one of the tents. Nobody slept very well. But the next morning was sunny, and everyone laughed about the wet night.

stories.title: My First Job
stories.text: When I was seventeen, I got my first job in a small restaurant. I worked there every Saturday and Sunday. My job was to wash the dishes and clean the tables. The work was hard, and I was always tired at the end of the day. But the cook was very kind, and he taught me how to make soup and salads. I earned a little money, and I saved most of it for a new bike. I still remember that job with a smile.

stories.title: The Talent Show
stories.text: Every year, our school has a talent show in June. This year, my friend Lucy decided to sing a song. She practised every day for two weeks, but she was very nervous before the show. When she walked onto the stage, her hands were shaking. Then the music started, and she sang beautifully. Everyone in the hall stood up and clapped. Lucy did not win first prize, but she felt very proud of herself.

stories.title: A Weekend in the Mountains
stories.text: Last month, my husband and I spent a weekend in the mountains. We stayed in a small wooden hotel next to a river. The air was fresh and cool, and it was very quiet. On Saturday, we walked for five hours and saw some beautiful lakes. We were very hungry when we came back, and the hotel served a delicious dinner. On Sunday, we relaxed and read our books. We want to go there again next year.

stories.title: The New Neighbours
stories.text: A new family moved into the house next to ours last week. They have two young children and a big brown dog. On Wednesday, my mother made a cake, and we took it to them. The parents were very friendly, and they invited us in for tea. They told us they came from Canada. Their daughter is the same age as me, and she is going to start at my school next Monday. I hope we can become friends.

stories.title: The Bike Accident
stories.text: On Friday afternoon, Sam was riding his bike home from school. It was raining, and the road was wet. Suddenly, a cat ran in front of him. Sam stopped quickly, but he fell off his bike and hurt his knee. A woman saw the accident and helped him. She called his parents, and his father came to get him. The doctor said his knee was fine. Now Sam always rides more slowly when it rains.

stories.title: A Wrong Number
stories.text: Last night, my phone rang at eleven o'clock. A man asked, "Is that Pizza Palace? I want to order a large pizza." I told him he had the wrong number. Ten minutes later, he called again with the same question. I explained politely that this was a private number. The next day, I looked on the internet. The pizza restaurant's number was almost the same as mine. Only one number was different!

stories.title: The Old Photo
stories.text: Last weekend, I was cleaning my room when I found an old photo in a box. It showed a young woman with long dark hair. She was standing next to a bicycle and smiling. I did not know who she was, so I showed the photo to my dad. He laughed and said, "That is your grandmother. She was twenty years old then." I was very surprised. Now the photo is on the wall in our living room.

stories.title: Waiting at the Airport
stories.text: Maria's brother lives in Australia, and she has not seen him for three years. Yesterday, he flew home for a visit. Maria went to the airport two hours early because she was so excited. She waited near the exit with a big sign with his name on it. The plane was forty minutes late, and she felt more nervous every minute. At last, she saw him come through the doors. They hugged for a long time and both cried a little.

stories.title: The Snow Day
stories.text: On Tuesday morning, Ben looked out of the window and saw that everything was white. There was a lot of snow, and the schools were closed. Ben put on his warm coat, his hat and his gloves, and he ran outside with his sister. They made a big snowman in the garden and gave it an old scarf. Then they played in the snow with their friends from next door. In the afternoon, their mother made hot chocolate for everyone.

stories.title: The Broken Window
stories.text: Tom and his friend Jack were playing football in the street after school. Jack kicked the ball very hard, and it flew into Mrs Green's window. The glass broke into small pieces. The boys were scared, and Jack wanted to run away. But Tom said, "No, we must tell her." They knocked on her door and said sorry. Mrs Green was not happy, but she was glad they were honest. The boys paid for the new window with their pocket money.

stories.title: Planting a Tree
stories.text: Last spring, our class planted a tree in the school garden. Our teacher bought a small apple tree from a shop near the school. First, two boys made a big hole in the ground. Then we put the tree in the hole and filled it with earth. Every student gave it some water. We take care of the tree every week, and now it is taller than me. Our teacher says that it is going to have apples next year.

stories.title: Visiting Grandparents
stories.text: Every summer, Anna visits her grandparents in a small village by the sea. Their house is old, but it is very comfortable. Her grandmother grows vegetables in the garden, and Anna helps her every morning. In the afternoons, they swim in the sea or walk along the beach. In the evenings, her grandfather tells funny stories about his life when he was young. Anna always feels sad when the holiday ends. She is already counting the days until next summer.

stories.title: A Day at the Market
stories.text: Every Saturday morning, my father and I go to the market in the town square. It is always busy and noisy. People sell fresh fruit, vegetables, fish, cheese and flowers. My father likes talking to the people at the market, and he knows many of them. Today we bought tomatoes, potatoes, a big melon and some honey. The honey seller gave me a small piece of cake for free. Our bags were very heavy, but we were happy with our shopping.

stories.title: The Fishing Trip
stories.text: Last Sunday, Uncle Peter took me fishing for the first time. We got up at five o'clock and drove to a quiet lake. Uncle Peter showed me how to put the fishing line in the water. Then we sat and waited for a long time. I was getting bored when suddenly something pulled my line. I caught a big fish! We took a photo of it, and then we put it back in the water. It was a wonderful day.

stories.title: Our Holiday Plans
stories.text: This summer, my family is going to travel to Spain for two weeks. We are going to fly to Barcelona and stay in a hotel near the beach. My mother wants to visit museums and old churches. My father is going to try a lot of Spanish food. My little sister just wants to swim in the sea every day. I am going to take a lot of photos with my new camera. We are all very excited about the trip.

stories.title: The Cinema Night
stories.text: On Friday evening, Leo and his friends went to the cinema to see a new film. They bought their tickets on the internet, so they did not need to wait in a long line. Before the film started, they got some popcorn and cold drinks. The film was about a group of children who travel to space. It was exciting and funny, and everyone enjoyed it. After the film, they went to a café and talked about their favourite parts.

stories.title: A Long Train Journey
stories.text: Last month, Sophie travelled by train from London to Edinburgh to visit her aunt. The journey took more than four hours. Sophie had a seat next to the window, so she could see the beautiful countryside. She saw green hills, small villages and lots of sheep. She read a magazine, listened to music and ate a sandwich. An old man sat opposite her, and they talked about books. When the train arrived, her aunt was waiting on the platform.

stories.title: The Science Project
stories.text: This month, Omar and his friend Lily had to do a science project together. They wanted to find out where plants grow fastest. They put three small plants in different places: one near the window, one in a dark cupboard and one in the kitchen. Every day, they measured the plants and wrote the results in a notebook. After three weeks, the plant near the window was the tallest. Their teacher liked their project and gave them a very good mark.

stories.title: Cleaning the House
stories.text: On Saturday morning, Mum said, "Your grandparents are coming for dinner tonight, and the house is a mess!" So everyone helped. Dad cleaned the floors, and my brother washed the windows. I tidied my bedroom and put all my clothes away. Then I helped Mum in the kitchen. By five o'clock, the house was clean and tidy. When my grandparents arrived, Grandma said, "What a lovely clean house!" We all smiled at each other.

stories.title: Breakfast in Bed
stories.text: Last Sunday was my mother's birthday, so my sister and I decided to make her breakfast in bed. We got up very early and went quietly to the kitchen. My sister made coffee and orange juice, and I made eggs and toast. We also put a small flower on the tray. Then we carried everything upstairs and knocked on her door. Mum was very surprised and happy. She said it was the best breakfast of her life.

stories.title: Running a Race
stories.text: Last year, my friend Kate started running three times a week. In April, she decided to enter a race of ten kilometres in our city. She trained hard for two months and ate healthy food. On the day of the race, the weather was hot, and there were more than a thousand runners. After seven kilometres, Kate was very tired, but she did not stop. She finished the race in less than an hour. She was very proud, and now she wants to run a longer race.

stories.title: The Restaurant Mistake
stories.text: Last Friday, Paul and his wife went to a new Italian restaurant for dinner. Paul ordered fish with vegetables, and his wife ordered a chicken salad. After twenty minutes, the waiter brought two big plates of pasta. Paul told him politely that they did not order pasta. The waiter was very sorry and took the plates back to the kitchen. Ten minutes later, he came back with the right food. The fish was delicious, and the restaurant did not ask them to pay for their drinks.

stories.title: A Kind Stranger
stories.text: Last winter, I was on my way home from work when my car stopped in the middle of the road. It was dark and very cold, and my phone battery was dead. I did not know what to do. Then a young man stopped his car and asked if I needed help. He called a garage on his phone and waited with me for an hour. When the mechanic arrived, I wanted to give the young man some money, but he said no. I will never forget his kindness.

stories.title: The New Haircut
stories.text: Emily always had long hair, but last week she decided to try something different. She went to a hairdresser near her house and asked for short hair. When she looked in the mirror, she was very surprised. She almost did not know herself! At first, she did not like it. But the next day at school, all her friends said her new hair looked great. Now Emily loves her short hair, and she thinks it is much easier to wash.

stories.title: Saving Money
stories.text: Jake is fifteen, and he really wants a new computer for his games. The computer costs six hundred pounds, but Jake only has fifty. His parents said they would pay for half of it if he saved the rest. So Jake made a plan. He started walking his neighbour's dog every day and washing cars at the weekend. He also stopped buying sweets and drinks after school. After eight months, he had enough money. Jake was very happy when he finally bought his computer.

stories.title: A Visit to the Castle
stories.text: During the school holidays, our family visited an old castle on a hill. It is more than eight hundred years old. A guide showed us around and told us about the people who lived there. We saw the big hall where the king had dinner with his guests. We also climbed some narrow stairs to the top of a tower. From there, we could see the whole town and the river. My little brother wanted to stay there all day!

stories.title: The Storm
stories.text: Last night, there was a terrible storm in our town. The wind was very strong, and it rained for hours. At about midnight, the lights went out, and we could not see anything. My father found some candles in a drawer, and we sat together in the living room. We heard loud thunder and saw lightning in the sky. In the morning, the storm was over. A big tree near our house was on the ground, but luckily nobody was hurt.

stories.title: Feeding the Birds
stories.text: In winter, it is hard for birds to find food. So every morning, my grandmother puts bread and seeds on the wall in her garden. Soon, lots of small birds come to eat. Some are brown, and some have red or yellow feathers. My grandmother knows the names of all of them. Last weekend, she gave me a small book about birds. Now I also feed the birds in my garden, and I write down the names of the ones I see.

stories.title: The Language Exchange
stories.text: Elif is learning English, and Tom is learning Turkish. They met on a language website a few months ago. Now they talk on video every Tuesday and Thursday. For thirty minutes, they speak English, and then they speak Turkish for thirty minutes. They help each other with grammar and new words. Sometimes they laugh at their mistakes. Last month, Tom visited Istanbul, and they finally met in person. They went to a café and talked for hours.

stories.title: The Wedding
stories.text: Last Saturday, my cousin Sara got married. The wedding was in a beautiful garden outside the city. Sara wore a long white dress, and her husband wore a dark blue suit. More than a hundred guests came. After the ceremony, we had a big dinner under the trees. Then a band played music, and everyone danced until midnight. My grandparents danced too, and everyone clapped for them. It was a long day, but it was the happiest day of the year.

stories.title: Showing a Friend Around
stories.text: Last week, my friend Carlos came from Mexico to visit me for five days. I wanted to show him the best places in my city. On the first day, we walked around the old town and visited a famous museum. On the second day, we took a boat trip on the river. Carlos loved the local food, especially the fish. On his last evening, we went up a hill and watched the sun go down. Carlos says he wants to come back next year.

stories.title: The Homework Problem
stories.text: On Sunday evening, Mia remembered that she had maths homework for Monday. It was already nine o'clock, and the homework was very difficult. She tried for an hour, but she could not answer the last three questions. She felt worried and almost cried. Then she called her friend Ella. Ella explained the questions slowly on the phone, and Mia finally understood them. She finished at half past ten. The next day, her teacher said her homework was perfect.

stories.title: Helping a Neighbour
stories.text: Mr Brown lives alone in the house next to ours. He is eighty years old, and last month he broke his leg. He could not go shopping or walk his dog. So my brother and I decided to help him. Every afternoon after school, we took his dog to the park. On Saturdays, we did his shopping at the supermarket. Mr Brown always gave us tea and biscuits and told us stories about his life. Now his leg is better, but we still visit him every week.

stories.title: A Week in Hospital
stories.text: Last spring, Oliver had a bad pain in his stomach, and his mother took him to the hospital. The doctor said he needed a small operation. Oliver was scared, but the nurses were very kind to him. The operation was quick, and after it, he stayed in the hospital for a week. His friends sent him cards and funny messages. His sister brought him books and his favourite chocolate. When he went home, he felt much better. He was happy to sleep in his own bed again.

stories.title: The Football Final
stories.text: Our school football team played in the final of the city cup last Saturday. Hundreds of students and parents came to watch. The other team was very good, and after twenty minutes, they scored a goal. In the second half, our team played much better, and Ali scored a goal for us. Then, two minutes before the end, our captain kicked the ball into the net. We won! Everyone ran onto the field and celebrated together.

stories.title: The Village Festival
stories.text: Every August, there is a big festival in the village where my grandparents live. People come from all the towns near the village. During the day, there are games for children, and farmers sell cheese, honey and fruit. In the evening, everyone eats together at long tables in the main square. After dinner, musicians play traditional songs, and people dance. This year, my cousins and I sold cakes at the festival. We sold more than fifty cakes, and we gave the money to the village school.

stories.title: Working From Home
stories.text: Since last spring, Hannah has worked from home three days a week. At first, she loved it because she did not have to travel to the office. She could start work in comfortable clothes and save money on transport. However, after a few months, she began to feel lonely. She missed chatting with her colleagues. Now she goes to a café near her flat on Fridays. Working there helps her concentrate, and she does not feel so alone.

stories.title: The Lost Luggage
stories.text: When Marco landed in Lisbon, he waited for his suitcase for almost an hour, but it never appeared. He went to the airline desk and filled in a form. The assistant explained that his bag had been sent to Madrid by mistake. Marco had to buy a toothbrush, a shirt and some socks. Luckily, the suitcase arrived at his hotel two days later. Since then, he has always packed spare clothes in his hand luggage.

stories.title: A Volunteer at the Animal Shelter
stories.text: Every Saturday morning, Lucy volunteers at an animal shelter outside her town. She has been doing this for two years. Her job is to feed the dogs, clean their cages and take them for walks. Some of the animals were found on the streets, so they are often frightened of people. Lucy is very patient with them. When a dog finds a new home, she feels sad but also proud. She says volunteering has made her a happier person.

stories.title: The Online Shopping Mistake
stories.text: Last month, Ben ordered a new jacket online. In the photo, it looked dark green and fashionable. When the parcel arrived a week later, he was disappointed. The jacket was bright yellow, and it was two sizes too big. He checked his order and realised that he had chosen the wrong size himself. Fortunately, the shop allowed customers to return items for free. Ben sent it back, and next time he will read the details more carefully.

stories.title: Living with Roommates
stories.text: When Jonas started university, he decided to share a flat with three other students. At first, it was fun because there was always someone to talk to. However, problems soon appeared. Nobody wanted to wash the dishes, and the kitchen was always dirty. One evening, they sat down together and made a list of jobs for each person. Since then, the flat has been much cleaner, and the four of them have become good friends.

stories.title: The Old Diary
stories.text: While she was cleaning the attic, Rosa found a small diary that had belonged to her grandmother. It was written more than sixty years ago, when her grandmother was a teenager. Rosa sat down and started reading. Her grandmother had written about her school, her best friend and a boy she liked. Rosa was surprised to discover how similar their lives were. That evening, she showed the diary to her mother, and they laughed and cried together.

stories.title: Learning to Swim as an Adult
stories.text: Peter is in his forties, but he has never learned to swim. As a child, he was afraid of water, and he always found reasons to avoid swimming lessons. Last year, his daughter asked him to come to the beach with her, and he felt embarrassed. So he decided to take lessons at the local pool. The first few weeks were difficult, but his teacher was very patient. Now he can swim fifty metres without stopping.

stories.title: The Street Musician
stories.text: Every evening, an old man plays the violin outside the main train station. Most people hurry past him, but a few stop to listen. Last week, a young woman stood there for a long time. When he finished, she told him that she was a music teacher. She invited him to play at a concert at her school. The man was so happy that he could hardly speak. Last Friday, two hundred children listened to him play.

stories.title: The Family Business
stories.text: Mr and Mrs Patel have run a small food shop in our street for twenty years. They open at seven in the morning and close at ten at night. Their children help them after school and at weekends. Although several large supermarkets have opened nearby, many people still prefer their shop. The Patels know every customer by name and always ask about their families. If someone forgets their money, they can pay the next day.

stories.title: The Exchange Student
stories.text: This year, our family is hosting an exchange student from Japan. Her name is Yuki, and she is sixteen. She will stay with us for six months and go to school with my sister. In the beginning, Yuki was very shy and spoke very little. But after a few weeks, she became more confident. She has taught us how to make sushi, and we have taken her to see castles and museums. We will all miss her when she leaves.

stories.title: The Job Promotion
stories.text: After five years at the same company, Laura was finally offered a promotion. Her manager asked her to lead a team of eight people. It was exciting news, but Laura was also worried. She had never been a manager before, and some of her colleagues were older than her. She decided to take a short course for new managers. Now, six months later, her team works well together, and Laura feels much more confident in her new role.

stories.title: The Lost Passport
stories.text: Two days before his flight home, Tom realised that his passport was missing. He searched his hotel room and his bags, but he could not find it anywhere. He started to panic. The hotel receptionist told him to go to the police and then to his embassy. The staff at the embassy were very helpful. They gave him an emergency passport the next morning, and he caught his flight on time. Now he always keeps a copy of his passport on his phone.

stories.title: The Community Garden
stories.text: A few years ago, there was an empty piece of land behind our block of flats. It was full of rubbish, and nobody used it. Then a group of neighbours decided to turn it into a garden. They cleaned the area, built wooden boxes and planted vegetables and flowers. Now people of all ages work there together. Children learn how food grows, and older people enjoy the fresh air. The garden has brought our neighbourhood closer together.

stories.title: Grandmother's Recipe
stories.text: When Elena's grandmother was alive, she made the best apple cake in the family. Unfortunately, she never wrote the recipe down. After she died, Elena tried to make the cake many times, but it never tasted the same. Last month, she found an old letter that her grandmother had sent to a friend. In the letter, there was the full recipe! Elena baked the cake for her mother's birthday, and everyone said it tasted exactly like the original.

stories.title: The Night Shift
stories.text: Michael works as a nurse in a large hospital, and this month he is working night shifts. He starts at nine in the evening and finishes at seven in the morning. The hospital is quieter at night, but there are still many patients who need help. The hardest part is sleeping during the day, because the city is so noisy. He uses thick curtains to keep his bedroom dark. Although the job is tiring, he says he loves helping people.

stories.title: A Difficult Decision
stories.text: Last year, Sara was offered a good job in another city. The salary was much higher, and the work sounded interesting. However, accepting it would mean leaving her family and friends. For several weeks, she could not decide what to do. She made a list of advantages and disadvantages and talked to people she trusted. In the end, she accepted the job. It was hard at first, but she has made new friends, and she visits her family every month.

stories.title: Moving Abroad
stories.text: Three years ago, Ahmed moved from Egypt to Canada to study engineering. Everything was different: the weather, the food and even the way people greeted each other. The first winter was very difficult because he had never seen so much snow. He also missed his family terribly. However, he joined a student club and met people from many countries. Now he speaks English very well, and he has decided to stay in Canada after he finishes university.

stories.title: Starting a Blog
stories.text: Last year, Nina started writing a blog about cheap travel. At first, only her friends read it. She wrote about places she had visited and gave advice on how to save money. She also added her own photos. Slowly, more and more people found her blog, and some of them sent her messages with questions. Now she has thousands of readers every month. A travel company has even asked her to write articles for their website.

stories.title: The Customer Complaint
stories.text: Mark works at the customer service desk of a large department store. One afternoon, an angry woman came to the desk. She had bought a coffee machine, but it had stopped working after two days. Mark listened to her carefully and apologised. He explained that she could choose between a new machine and her money back. The woman calmed down and chose a new one. Before leaving, she thanked Mark for being so polite and patient.

stories.title: The School Reunion
stories.text: Twenty years after they finished school, Paula's old classmates organised a reunion. Paula was nervous because she had not seen most of them since she was eighteen. When she arrived at the restaurant, she hardly recognised some people. Others had not changed at all. They looked at old photos and laughed about their teachers and school trips. Paula was surprised to learn that her best friend from school now lived in her town. They have met every week since then.

stories.title: The Broken Phone Screen
stories.text: Last Tuesday, Emma dropped her phone on the floor of the bus, and the screen broke. She could still use it, but it was difficult to read her messages. A new phone was too expensive, so she looked for a repair shop. The man in the shop said he could replace the screen in an hour. It cost forty pounds, which was much cheaper than she had expected. Since then, she has kept her phone in a strong case.

stories.title: Recycling at Home
stories.text: A year ago, the Wilson family decided to produce less rubbish. They bought three different bins: one for paper, one for plastic and glass, and one for food waste. At first, the children often forgot which bin to use. Their mother put colourful signs on each bin to help them. Now everyone sorts their rubbish without thinking about it. They also try to buy products with less packaging. Their rubbish bag is now half the size it used to be.

stories.title: A Surprise Visit
stories.text: Carla had been living in London for two years when she decided to surprise her parents in Spain. She did not tell anyone except her brother. She bought a ticket and flew home on a Friday evening. When she rang the bell, her mother opened the door and screamed with joy. Her father was so surprised that he dropped his cup of coffee. They spent the whole weekend cooking, talking and laughing together. It was the best weekend Carla had had in years.

stories.title: Fixing the Bicycle
stories.text: When Leo found his grandfather's old bicycle in the garage, it was covered in dust, and the tyres were flat. He decided to repair it himself. He watched several videos online to learn how to do it. First, he cleaned the whole bike and replaced the tyres. Then he fixed the brakes and the chain. It took him three weekends, but finally the bike was ready. Now he rides it to school every day, and his grandfather is very proud of him.

stories.title: The Wrong Train
stories.text: Last summer, Julia was travelling around Italy by train. One morning, she was in a hurry and got on a train without checking the information carefully. After an hour, she realised that she did not recognise the names of the stations. She asked the passenger next to her, who told her that the train was going to Naples, not Florence. Julia got off at the next station and waited two hours for another train. Although she was annoyed, she enjoyed a delicious pizza while she waited.

stories.title: A New Hobby: Painting
stories.text: After he retired, Mr Kim did not know how to spend his free time. His wife suggested that he should try painting. At first, he was not sure, because he had not painted since he was at school. However, he joined a class at the local community centre. He learned how to mix colours and paint landscapes. Now he paints almost every day, and some of his pictures have been shown at a small exhibition in the town library.

stories.title: The Second-Hand Bookshop
stories.text: In the old part of town, there is a small shop that sells used books. The owner, Mrs Grant, has run it for more than thirty years. The shelves go up to the ceiling, and there are books everywhere, even on the stairs. Customers often spend hours there looking for rare books. Mrs Grant knows exactly where every book is, although nothing seems to be in order. Many students come because the books are much cheaper than in other shops.

stories.title: The Noisy Hotel
stories.text: For their holiday, Tim and Anna booked a hotel that promised a quiet room with a sea view. However, when they arrived, they discovered that their room was above a nightclub. The music continued until four in the morning, and they could not sleep. The next day, they complained to the manager. He apologised and moved them to a room on the top floor at the other side of the building. The rest of the holiday was peaceful and relaxing.

stories.title: A Healthy Breakfast Habit
stories.text: For many years, David never ate breakfast. He usually drank a large coffee on the way to work and felt hungry by eleven o'clock. Then he often ate biscuits and chocolate at his desk. His doctor told him that a healthy breakfast would give him more energy. So David started eating porridge with fruit every morning. After a few weeks, he noticed that he felt less tired, and he did not want sweet snacks any more. He has also lost some weight.

stories.title: The Hiking Accident
stories.text: Last autumn, Ryan and his friend went hiking in the mountains. On the way down, Ryan slipped on a wet rock and hurt his ankle badly. He could not walk, and there was no phone signal. His friend gave him water and a warm jacket and then walked for an hour to find help. Two hours later, a rescue team arrived and carried Ryan down the mountain. The doctor said his ankle was not broken. Now Ryan always tells someone where he is going before a hike.

stories.title: The Online Course
stories.text: Last winter, Maria decided to learn Spanish, but she did not have time to go to evening classes. Instead, she signed up for an online course. Every evening after dinner, she watched short videos and did exercises on her laptop. Once a week, she had a video lesson with a teacher from Mexico. At first, she found it hard to study alone without other students. However, after six months, she was able to have simple conversations in Spanish.

stories.title: The Garden Party
stories.text: Every summer, our neighbours, the Johnsons, have a garden party for the whole street. This year, it nearly did not happen because the weather forecast said it would rain. Mr Johnson put up a large tent just in case. In the end, the sun came out in the afternoon, and more than forty people came. There was music, food from many different countries and games for the children. Everyone agreed that it had been the best party so far.

stories.title: Saving Energy at Home
stories.text: When their electricity bill arrived in January, the Brown family were very surprised. It was twice as high as the year before. They decided to make some changes. They switched off lights when they left a room and stopped leaving the TV on all night. They also put on warm jumpers instead of turning up the heating. After three months, their bill was much lower. The children even started reminding their parents to turn things off.

stories.title: The Wedding Speech
stories.text: When Daniel's best friend asked him to give a speech at his wedding, he immediately said yes. But as the day came closer, he became more and more nervous. He had never spoken in front of so many people before. He wrote the speech carefully and practised it in front of the mirror every evening. On the day, his hands were shaking at first. But when the guests laughed at his first joke, he relaxed. After the speech, everyone stood up and clapped.

stories.title: The Dog Walker
stories.text: Sophie is a university student who needed some extra money. Because she loves animals, she offered to walk dogs for people in her neighbourhood. She put a small notice in the local shop, and soon five families contacted her. Now she walks the dogs twice a day, before and after her lectures. It keeps her fit, and she earns enough money to pay for her books. The only problem is that she has to go out even when it is raining.

stories.title: Looking for a Flat
stories.text: After he got a new job in the city, Omar needed to find a flat quickly. He looked at websites every day and visited more than ten flats in two weeks. Some were too expensive, and others were too far from his office. One flat looked lovely in the photos, but in reality it was dark and small. Finally, he found a bright flat with a balcony, only ten minutes from work. He signed the contract the same day.

stories.title: The Cooking Class
stories.text: For her birthday, Lena's brother gave her a ticket for a cooking class at a famous restaurant. The class took place on a Saturday afternoon, and there were eight other people in the group. The chef showed them how to make fresh pasta and a simple tomato sauce. Lena had always bought pasta in packets, so she was surprised how easy it was. At the end, everyone ate what they had cooked together. Since then, Lena has made her own pasta several times.

stories.title: The Book Club
stories.text: Two years ago, Helen joined a book club at her local library. The members meet on the first Monday of every month to discuss a book they have all read. Helen enjoys hearing different opinions about the same story. Thanks to the club, she has read books that she would not normally choose, such as science fiction and history. She has also made some good friends there. Next month, it is her turn to choose the book.

stories.title: The Charity Run
stories.text: Last spring, the staff of a small company decided to raise money for a hospital for sick children in their town. They organised a run of five kilometres in the park and asked friends and family to support them. Most of them had not run for years, so they trained together after work. On the day, more than sixty people took part. Everyone finished the race, even the boss, who walked most of the way. Together they raised over two thousand pounds.

stories.title: The Tennis Match
stories.text: Every Sunday morning, Ana plays tennis with her old friend Rita. They have played together since they were at school, and Rita almost always wins. Last Sunday, however, something unusual happened. Ana had been practising hard all week, and she played better than ever. The match was very close, and it lasted almost two hours. In the end, Ana won the final point. Rita laughed and shook her hand, and then they went for coffee as usual.

stories.title: A Career Change
stories.text: After working as an accountant for twelve years, Mark realised that he no longer enjoyed his job. He had always been passionate about cooking, so he decided to train as a chef. Many of his friends thought he was making a terrible mistake, especially since he would earn far less at first. The training was physically demanding, and he often worked until midnight. Nevertheless, he has never regretted his decision. If he had stayed in his old job, he would never have discovered what truly makes him happy.

stories.title: The Tiny House
stories.text: Rising rents in the city convinced Julia and her partner to try something unusual: they built a tiny house on a piece of land owned by her uncle. The house is only twenty square metres, so they had to get rid of most of their belongings. At first, they struggled to adjust to such a small space. However, they gradually discovered that owning fewer things actually made them feel freer. They now spend far less money and much more time outdoors.

stories.title: The Gap Year
stories.text: Instead of going straight to university, Tom decided to take a year off. He spent the first six months working in a supermarket to save money, and then he travelled across South America. He volunteered on an organic farm, learned basic Spanish and met people with very different lifestyles. His parents had been worried that he would lose interest in studying. In fact, the opposite happened: he returned with a much clearer idea of what he wanted to study and why.

stories.title: The Viral Video
stories.text: Last month, Priya posted a short video of her grandmother dancing at a family wedding. She had only intended to share it with a few relatives, but somehow it spread across social media. Within three days, it had been viewed more than two million times. Journalists contacted the family, and her grandmother was even invited onto a television show.
